languages.name: Prolog

categories.name: Facts, Rules, and Queries

entries.title: Facts
entries.summary: Declare statements that are unconditionally true in the knowledge base.

entries.title: Rules
entries.summary: Define conclusions that hold when other goals succeed.
entries.definition: Define conclusions that hold when other goals succeed.
entries.mental_model: A rule is an implication Prolog can use backward from a goal.

entries.title: Queries
entries.summary: Ask Prolog to prove a goal and bind variables that satisfy it.

entries.title: Variables
entries.summary: Represent unknown values using identifiers that begin with uppercase letters or underscores.
entries.definition: Represent unknown values using identifiers that begin with uppercase letters or underscores.
entries.mental_model: Variables begin unbound and become constrained through unification.

entries.title: Atoms and compound terms
entries.summary: Represent symbolic constants and structured values.
entries.definition: Represent symbolic constants and structured values.
entries.mental_model: Compound terms are lightweight structured trees.

entries.title: Unification
entries.summary: Make two terms identical by binding variables where possible.
entries.definition: Make two terms identical by binding variables where possible.
entries.mental_model: Unification is pattern matching that can bind both sides.

entries.title: Backtracking
entries.summary: Explore alternative clauses or choices when later goals fail.
entries.definition: Explore alternative clauses or choices when later goals fail.
entries.mental_model: The engine keeps choice points and rewinds to try another path.

examples.explanation: Prolog can yield red and then blue on backtracking.

entries.title: Cut (!)
entries.summary: Commit to choices made before the cut in the current predicate.
entries.definition: Commit to choices made before the cut in the current predicate.
entries.gotchas: Overusing cut can make logic harder to reason about.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: Negation as failure
entries.summary: Succeed when a goal cannot be proven.
entries.definition: Succeed when a goal cannot be proven.
entries.mental_model: This is failure-to-prove, not classical logical negation.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: safe/1 succeeds when blocked/1 cannot be proven.

entries.title: once/1
entries.summary: Run a goal but keep only its first solution.
entries.definition: Run a goal but keep only its first solution.
entries.mental_model: Keep the first proof and discard later alternatives.

categories.name: Lists and Recursion
categories.description: Recursive data processing and collection predicates.

entries.title: Lists
entries.mental_model: A list is either [] or one head element plus another list.

entries.title: Recursive predicates
entries.summary: Define behavior in terms of smaller versions of the same problem.
entries.definition: Define behavior in terms of smaller versions of the same problem.
entries.mental_model: State the base case, then reduce the problem.

entries.title: member/2
entries.summary: Relate an item to a list containing it.

categories.description: Practical logic patterns for project helpers.

entries.title: Dependency rules
entries.summary: Model dependencies as facts and derive transitive relationships recursively.
entries.definition: Model dependencies as facts and derive transitive relationships recursively.
entries.mental_model: Represent the graph as facts and let recursion walk it.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
depends(app, parser).
depends(parser, lexer).
needs(A, B) :- depends(A, B).
needs(A, B) :- depends(A, X), needs(X, B).

entries.title: Capability selection
entries.summary: Select tools or actions by declaring required and provided capabilities.
entries.definition: Select tools or actions by declaring required and provided capabilities.
entries.mental_model: Describe constraints, then query for satisfying choices.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
provides(zig, native_build).
needs(build, native_build).
usable(Task, Tool) :- needs(Task, C), provides(Tool, C).
